title: mssql ConnectionError
body: I'm using Deno 1.37.0 with npm:mssql@10.0.1 to connect to SQL Server at localhost:1433 in a Docker container, with trustServerCertificate enabled. The connection times out after 15000ms, while the equivalent code works with Node 18.16.0. I instrumented tedious: Node connects, negotiates ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 with TLS 1.2, logs in, and executes requests; Deno connects and reaches SentTLSSSLNegotiation but then times out and closes.

symptoms_visible: My Deno connection to localhost:1433 times out after 15000ms, although the equivalent Node 18.16.0 program connects and runs the stored procedure.
The instrumented Node run negotiates TLS 1.2 and logs in; the Deno run reaches SentTLSSSLNegotiation, waits, and then closes.
N0.label: N0 encrypted mssql connection stalls

symptoms_visible: The mssql connection still stalls during TLS negotiation.
openssl connects to port 1433 but reads zero handshake bytes and reports an unexpected EOF with no peer certificate.
The SQL Server container logs error 17821 saying that no valid TLS certificate is configured for strict TDS 8.0-and-above connections.
N1.label: N1 raw TLS probes collected

symptoms_visible: With Deno 1.40.1 and mssql 10.0.2, I see deprecated Deno.TcpConn.rid warnings and the connection still times out at localhost:1433 after 15000ms.
N2_x.label: N2_x ordinary version upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: On my last tested Deno setup, encrypted mssql connections still reach the TLS-negotiation state and then time out.
N3.label: N3 Node-compatibility root cause identified

symptoms_visible: The last result from my own Docker setup is still the encrypted mssql timeout, and I have not posted a canary retest. A different affected user reports that the canary build works.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available but original reporter not verified

question_patterns: Could you run openssl s_client against the database address and paste its raw output?
Could you run a minimal Deno.connectTls probe against the same host and port and report what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran both against localhost:1433 with Deno 1.38.3. openssl says CONNECTED, then 'unexpected eof while reading'; it read 0 bytes, received no peer certificate, and selected no cipher. I also ran the minimal Deno.connectTls code against that address.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both openssl and Deno.connectTls complete a normal TLS handshake, receive the server certificate, and negotiate the same TLS 1.2 cipher as Node.
The probes cannot open a TCP connection at all because localhost:1433 refuses the connection and the Docker port is not published.
The same unexpected-EOF output occurs when I use 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost.

question_patterns: What exact certificate, cipher, and byte-count details does openssl print?
Please paste the complete openssl handshake summary rather than interpreting it.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It prints 'no peer certificate available', 'SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 302 bytes', and 'Cipher is (NONE)', followed by verification code 0.

question_patterns: Do the SQL Server container logs record anything when you run these probes?
Can you check the database-side log at the timestamp of the failed connection?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The container logs: 'Error: 17821, Severity: 20, State: 1. A valid TLS certificate is not configured to accept strict (TDS 8.0 and above) connections. The connection has been closed.'

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The server log shows that the client completed prelogin and TLS successfully, but SQL authentication rejected the username and password.

edges.comment: Reporter c9-c10 on the reporter's Docker SQL Server: participant2 requested raw openssl and Deno.connectTls probes; the reporter pasted the openssl output and then independently added the contemporaneous SQL Server error 17821 log. These are raw measurements, not proof of the eventual duplex-stream diagnosis.

solution.intent: Try a routine Deno upgrade in case newer Node-compatibility or TLS code already resolves the mssql timeout.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade from Deno 1.38.x to the current stable Deno 1.40.1, update mssql, and rerun the same connection.

edges.comment: Reporter c12, describing only the reporter's system: the reporter had upgraded to Deno 1.40.1 and mssql 10.0.2, but the same 15000ms timeout remained. The upgrade is therefore a real falsified attempt, not the resolution.

solution.intent: Diagnose the failure as a Deno Node-compatibility limitation: mssql/tedious starts TLS over a duplex stream, while Deno's internal TLS termination supports only a TCP stream and cannot operate on the fake net.Socket expected by Node internals.
solution.concrete_example: The connection is not failing at TCP reachability or SQL authentication. mssql terminates TLS on a duplex stream, but Deno can currently terminate TLS only on a TCP stream. Deno needs a bridge that exposes the duplex as the fake net.Socket Node internals expect while allowing Rust TLS code to read and write it.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter's logs localize the stall to the transition after TDS prelogin, but they do not themselves establish Deno's internal stream limitation. Participant16 supplied the accepted implementation diagnosis in c30: mssql terminates TLS on a duplex, Deno supported termination only on TCP, and Node internals expected the duplex to behave like a fake net.Socket.

edges.comment: Maintainer diagnosis c30. This is the final accepted technical explanation after the long multi-party discussion. The Azure SQL and PostgreSQL reports are not merged into the reporter's Docker-system causal chain.

solution.intent: Ship the Deno Node-compatibility implementation that permits TLS termination over the duplex/fake-net.Socket path used by mssql, then ask the original reporter to retest encrypted mssql on a build containing that fix.
solution.concrete_example: The compatibility fix is available in canary. Upgrade a test installation with 'deno upgrade canary', rerun the original encrypted mssql configuration without disabling encryption, and report whether the stored procedure now executes; return to stable afterward if needed.
solution.inference_hint: At the thread tail, a maintainer clarified that the fix was available only in canary, and participant12 then reported 'canary works'. That is verification by a different affected operator, not by the original reporter, so it must not be presented as the reporter's own successful retest.

edges.comment: Thread c34-c36: participant9 suggested testing canary, participant18 confirmed the fix was only there, and participant12 reported that canary worked. This evidence comes from a different affected user's setup. The original reporter's last message was c28 and contains no post-fix retest, so user_perceives_resolved remains false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: mssql/tedious terminates TLS on a duplex stream, while Deno's Node-compatibility internals supported TLS termination only on a TCP stream and lacked the required duplex-to-fake-net.Socket bridge.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: Node completes TLS 1.2 and logs in against the same database, while Deno reaches SentTLSSSLNegotiation and times out; the requested openssl and server-side logs provide additional raw observations.
Must not treat an ordinary upgrade to Deno 1.40.1 as the fix, because the reporter tried it and still received the same timeout.
The technical fix must support the encrypted mssql duplex path rather than relying on disabling encryption.

Must ask the original reporter to verify the connection on a build containing the fix before declaring their case resolved. A different affected user's successful canary test is supporting evidence but is not the reporter's own verification.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable application developer: can reproduce behavior in Node and Deno, vendor npm dependencies, instrument tedious internals, compare protocol state logs, inspect Docker logs, and run openssl or canary builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and evidence-driven; supplies code and raw logs, follows diagnostic instructions, and periodically asks for progress without overstating conclusions.
